financials_interim.notes: COMPANY (standalone/holding-company-only, equity-method) basis. Same period as GROUP row -- see GROUP row's notes for shared context (IPO, subsequent-event acquisition, consolidation-lag caveat for the Life Insurance subsidiary applies at Group level only). AT THIS COMPANY LEVEL, per the task's holding-company check: JXG's standalone P&L is OVERWHELMINGLY dominated by 'Share of profit/(loss) from equity accounted investee (net of tax)' -- i.e. its equity-method pickup of Janashakthi Insurance PLC, Janashakthi Finance PLC and First Capital Holdings PLC -- rather than by trading revenue. Company Revenue is a nominal Rs.76,621k this quarter (2025: nil, an immaterial new revenue line, not itemised further); by contrast the equity-accounted share swung from a Rs.2,097,835k GAIN in Q1 FY2025/26 to a Rs.(241,510)k LOSS in Q1 FY2026/27, a swing of Rs.2,339,345k, which alone drives essentially all of the movement in Company Profit Before Tax (Rs.(617,092)k vs Rs.1,509,676k, a Rs.2,126,768k unfavourable swing -- close to, though not exactly, the equity-pickup swing, with the balance explained by Profit from operations improving to Rs.38,397k (2025: Rs.(111,327)k loss) on higher Other Operating Income and FVTPL gains at Company level, and Net finance cost narrowing to Rs.(413,979)k from Rs.(476,832)k). Investment in subsidiaries (Rs.22,069,319k, Note 4, page 7) represents 70.5% of Company Total Assets (Rs.31,294,052k) -- confirming JXG's standalone balance sheet is fundamentally a holding vehicle for its equity-accounted stakes: Janashakthi Insurance PLC (77.58%, carrying value Rs.13,161,583k), Janashakthi Finance PLC (93.44%, Rs.3,544,052k), First Capital Holdings PLC (76.57%, Rs.5,363,684k). Profit/(Loss) attributable to Equity Holders of the Company at GROUP level (Rs.(617,092)k) is IDENTICAL to Company-level PAT (Rs.(617,092)k) -- expected, since both represent the same economic parent-company profit computed via different consolidation techniques (full consolidation net of NCI at Group level vs. equity method at Company level); this equality was used as a cross-check and ties exactly. tax_expense=0 (Income tax (expense)/reversal is 'nil' for the Company both periods -- the Company itself pays no direct tax on its equity-accounted income, which is already presented net of the underlying subsidiaries' tax). eps_basic=eps_diluted=(0.30) (2025: 2.38), identical to the GROUP row's EPS (expected, since it is the same PAT-attributable-to-equity-holders and same weighted-average share base) -- see GROUP row's notes for the share-count/subdivision comparability caveat, which applies equally here. gross_profit=76,621=Revenue (no Cost of Sales line disclosed for the Company). trade_receivables=248,260 / trade_payables=469,657 map to 'Trade, other receivables and advances' / 'Trade and other payables' -- not pure trade-only figures, same caveat as GROUP row. short_term_borrowings=6,413,560 = Note 7 Current Borrowings (5,645,574) + Bank overdrafts (767,986); long_term_borrowings=7,703,972 = Note 7 Non-Current Borrowings. Debentures (Rs.1,292,657k) excluded from both fields for the same reason as the GROUP row. current_assets/current_liabilities left blank -- same BS-format gap as GROUP row (no current/non-current subtotal presented).

GROUP basis. Janashakthi PLC (JXG) is a listed holding company (Principal Activities: 'Investment and Management of Subsidiaries') whose Group results FULLY CONSOLIDATE its subsidiaries -- Janashakthi Insurance PLC (77.58% held, life insurance), Janashakthi Finance PLC (93.44%, NBFI/leasing), First Capital Holdings PLC (76.57%, investment banking/primary dealer/asset management), and Janashakthi Corporate Services Ltd (100%). At GROUP level the P&L is genuine consolidated trading income (Revenue Rs.6,400,178k from insurance premiums, NBFI interest, investment banking activity -- see Note 8 segments), NOT dominated by an equity-accounted associate line (that line is nil at Group level; it only appears in the COMPANY row, see that row's notes for the Company-level equity-pickup dynamic). Q1 FY2026/27 (three months ended 30 June 2026) vs Q1 FY2025/26 (three months ended 30 June 2025) comparative, both presented on the face P&L (page 3). MATERIAL CONSOLIDATION CAVEAT (filing footnote, repeated on every statement): 'Janashakthi Insurance PLC's 31 March 2026 financial information was used for Group consolidation as at 30 June 2026 due to its differing financial year-end (31 December)' -- i.e. the Life Insurance segment (39% of quarter Revenue, by far the largest asset base) is consolidated with a ~3-month lag and does NOT reflect the insurer's actual 30 June 2026 position; the same lag convention is presumably applied consistently to the 30 June 2025 comparative, which preserves YoY comparability of trend but means neither period is a true 'as at quarter-end' consolidated position for that segment -- flagged as a structural feature of this filing, not an error. Segment note (Note 8, page 10) is DISCLOSED ONLY for the current quarter (no 2025 comparator column), so segment-level YoY analysis is not possible from this filing (see gaps_note); however the CURRENT-QUARTER segment split is still informative: of the Group's Rs.(780,766)k net loss, Investment Banking (First Capital Holdings) contributed the single largest loss at Rs.(689,291)k, followed by 'Other' at Rs.(366,496)k, while Life Insurance (Rs.234,064k) and NBFI (Rs.90,414k) segments were BOTH profitable this quarter -- i.e. the Group loss is concentrated in the investment-banking/trading book, not the insurance or lending franchises. Revenue by segment (quarter only): Life Insurance Rs.2,475,340k (39%), Investment Banking Rs.2,102,945k (33%), NBFI Rs.1,832,133k (29%), Other Rs.78,217k, Eliminations Rs.(88,457)k. PRESENTATION CAVEAT: 'Gross profit' (Rs.3,868,159k, -14.5% YoY from Rs.4,523,016k) is Revenue less Cost of sales and direct expenses ONLY -- insurance claims/ benefits, underwriting/acquisition costs and the change in life-fund contract liabilities (combined Rs.2,506,407k, +25.0% YoY from Rs.2,005,582k) are presented as a SEPARATE 'Benefits and losses' subtotal below Gross Profit, not netted into Cost of Sales -- so this 'gross profit' is not comparable to a non-insurer's gross margin. DOMINANT DRIVER OF THE SWING TO AN OPERATING LOSS: Change in fair value of financial assets at FVTPL swung Rs.2,229,334k unfavourably, from a Rs.1,256,464k GAIN in Q1 FY2025/26 to a Rs.972,870k LOSS in Q1 FY2026/27 -- mark-to-market volatility on the Group's Rs.87,951,342k FVTPL portfolio (government securities, quoted equities, unit trusts, debentures -- Note 5.1, page 8), concentrated in the insurance and investment-banking books. Other Operating Income also fell Rs.1,248,751k (Rs.114,356k vs Rs.1,363,107k, -91.6%). Together these two items account for ~74% of the Rs.4,707,850k swing in Profit/(Loss) from operations (Rs.(1,248,675)k vs Rs.3,459,175k); the remainder reflects higher net insurance benefits/claims (+Rs.500,825k, +25.0%) and higher Administrative & other operating expenses (+Rs.135,801k, +9.3% to Rs.1,598,161k), partly offset by lower Selling & distribution expenses (-Rs.76,668k, -56.8%). Below the operating line, Net finance income/(cost) swung FAVOURABLY from a Rs.408,781k net expense to a Rs.304,566k net income (+Rs.713,347k), driven by Finance income surging to Rs.764,097k (2025: Rs.12,042k, +6,246%) -- likely investment-banking-book interest/repo income growth, consistent with the Investment Banking segment's Rs.2,102,945k quarter revenue -- which partially offset the operating-line deterioration. Income tax swung from a Rs.869,782k EXPENSE to a Rs.163,343k net REVERSAL/ credit (a Rs.1,033,125k favourable swing), further cushioning the bottom line. tax_expense is stored as -163,343 (a NEGATIVE value, i.e. a net credit, not an expense) so that Profit Before Tax (-944,109) minus tax_expense (-163,343) ties exactly to Profit After Tax (-780,766) -- this is a deliberate sign convention for this row, flagged here since other symbols in this database store tax_expense as a positive magnitude (genuine expense); JXG Group this quarter is a genuine net credit. finance_income=764,097 / finance_costs=459,531 stored from the face P&L split (both disclosed, unlike ASPH/BPPL where only a net line was given). EPS CAVEAT (important comparability flag): eps_basic=eps_diluted=(0.30) uses the WEIGHTED-AVERAGE share count during the quarter, not the 2,300,000,000 shares in issue at 30 June 2026 -- the Company completed an IPO of 500,000,000 new shares on 29 April 2026 (within this quarter), so the weighted-average count is lower (approx. 2.14bn); cross-check -617,092,000/2,300,000,000=-0.268/share vs disclosed -0.30, consistent with a lower weighted-average base. SEPARATELY, and more materially: the prior-year comparative EPS of 2.38 (Q1 FY2025/26) was computed on the PRE-SUBDIVISION share count of 633,551,428 (cross-check: 1,509,677,000/633,551,428=2.383, exact match) -- the Company's 31 December 2025 share subdivision (2.84 shares for each existing share, per the Shareholders Information note, page 12) does NOT appear to have been applied retrospectively to restate the 2025 comparative EPS as LKAS 33 would normally require. This means the eps_basic YoY comparison (-0.30 vs 2.38) is NOT like-for-like -- roughly 3.6x of the apparent EPS decline is a share-count base effect (subdivision + IPO), not economic profit decline; the underlying PAT swing (-780,766 vs 2,180,612, Group; or -617,092 vs 1,509,677 attributable to equity holders) is the cleaner metric and is what is used for the profit_after_tax metric in yoy_json. Cross-check: shares_in_issue (2,300,000,000, Shareholder Information note, page 11) x NAV/share (6.64) = Rs.15,272,000,000 vs disclosed Total equity attributable to shareholders of the company Rs.15,272,997k -- matches to rounding. current_assets/current_liabilities are left BLANK: this Statement of Financial Position (page 2) does NOT present a current/non-current subtotal split (standard practice for insurers/ financial-services groups presenting by order of liquidity per SLFRS), a genuine filing-format gap, not an omission. inventory=17,667 (a small, non-insurance-related stock balance, likely NBFI repossessed assets or similar -- not itemised further). trade_receivables=3,552,873 maps to 'Trade, other receivables and advances' (not a pure trade-only figure -- includes 'advances'). trade_payables=7,579,701 maps to 'Trade and other payables'. short_term_borrowings=27,246,849 = Note 7 Current Borrowings (24,253,112) + Bank overdrafts (2,993,737); long_term_borrowings=17,356,884 = Note 7 Non-Current Borrowings. NOT included in either borrowings field, to avoid mischaracterising distinct disclosed funding lines: Securities sold under repurchase agreements (Rs.52,768,305k, First Capital Holdings' primary-dealer repo book -- larger than total interest-bearing borrowings) and Deposits from customers (Rs.17,771,774k, Janashakthi Finance's NBFI deposit book); Debentures (Rs.7,316,156k, Note 6, tenors 2-5 years) are also excluded from both borrowings fields since the face BS does not split them current/non-current -- all three are material additional funding sources for this financial-services group, cited here rather than folded into the standard fields. capex=44,965 = Acquisition of property, plant and equipment (cash flow statement, page 6). MATERIAL SUBSEQUENT EVENT (Note 11, page 11, dated 13 August 2026, after the 30 June 2026 quarter-end): JXG entered a Share Purchase Agreement with Melstacorp PLC to acquire 100% of Continental Insurance Lanka Limited for LKR 5.2bn (81% initial controlling stake, then 9% in year one and 10% in year two), subject to IRCSL approval -- a material insurance-sector consolidation move funded in part by the Rs.5,000,000k raised via the April 2026 IPO (Stated Capital rose from Rs.4,300,000k to Rs.9,300,000k in this quarter).

thesis.thesis_text: Janashakthi PLC is a financial-services holding company that fully consolidates Janashakthi Insurance PLC (77.58%, life insurance), Janashakthi Finance PLC (93.44%, NBFI/leasing) and First Capital Holdings PLC (76.57%, investment banking/primary dealer). Group swung to a Rs.780.8mn net loss in Q1 FY2026/27 (from a Rs.2,180.6mn profit a year earlier), driven by a Rs.2,229.3mn unfavourable swing in FVTPL fair-value gains and a Rs.1,248.8mn drop in Other Operating Income -- concentrated in the Investment Banking segment (Rs.689.3mn loss), while Life Insurance (+Rs.234.1mn) and NBFI (+Rs.90.4mn) stayed profitable. The reported EPS collapse (Rs.2.38 to Rs.(0.30)) is not like-for-like given an unrestated December 2025 share subdivision and a mid-quarter IPO, so the underlying PAT swing is the cleaner read. At Rs.11.00, P/B (on parent-attributable equity, Rs.6.64/share NAV) is a moderate 1.66x; the Group is now pursuing a material post-quarter acquisition of Continental Insurance Lanka for Rs.5.2bn, subject to regulatory approval (Q1 FY2026/27 filing, source_doc_id 52751).
thesis.gaps_note: Macro & Industry Outlook (10% weight) unavailable -- no CBSL/IRCSL/insurance-sector data source exists in this project; the remaining five pillars are renormalized to sum to 100% (Financial Quality 33.3%, Growth 22.2%, Valuation 22.2%, Business Quality 16.7%, Governance & Risk 5.6%). Confidence is limited: only ONE interim quarter is on file (no annual report review, no multi-period trend), the Group's structure is complex (Life Insurance subsidiary consolidated with a ~3-month reporting lag, an unrestated share subdivision distorting EPS comparability, and a pending material acquisition not yet reflected in these financials), and only one year of dividend data (FY2025) is available.

financial_quality.rationale: Group swung from a Rs.2,180.6mn profit to a Rs.780.8mn loss, driven by a Rs.2,229.3mn unfavourable swing in FVTPL fair-value gains (Rs.1,256.5mn gain to Rs.972.9mn loss) on an Rs.87,951.3mn investment portfolio and a Rs.1,248.8mn drop in Other Operating Income -- genuine earnings volatility rather than a franchise problem, since Life Insurance (+Rs.234.1mn) and NBFI (+Rs.90.4mn) segments both stayed profitable. High leverage (borrowings, repo book of Rs.52,768.3mn, and deposits of Rs.17,771.8mn) is structurally normal for an insurance/NBFI/investment-banking group, not a standalone red flag.

growth_outlook.rationale: Group revenue fell 11.6% YoY to Rs.6,400.2mn and the Group swung to a net loss, but this quarter's deterioration is concentrated in the Investment Banking segment's trading book (Rs.689.3mn loss) rather than the core insurance/lending franchises. A material post-quarter growth catalyst exists: a Rs.5.2bn agreement (13 August 2026) to acquire Continental Insurance Lanka from Melstacorp PLC, partly funded by the Rs.5.0bn IPO completed this quarter, subject to IRCSL approval -- a genuine expansion opportunity, though unproven and execution-dependent.

valuation.rationale: P/E is not meaningful this quarter given the Rs.780.8mn Group net loss. Using parent-attributable equity of Rs.15,272,997k / 2,300,000,000 shares = NAV/share of Rs.6.64 (the group total equity of Rs.21,333,493k includes non-controlling interests in the majority-but-not-wholly-owned subsidiaries and is not the right denominator), P/B at Rs.11.00 (2026-08-28) is a moderate ~1.66x for a group spanning insurance, NBFI and investment banking. FY2025 DPS was Rs.3.06, but only one year of dividend history exists, and this quarter's loss makes near-term payout capacity uncertain.

business_quality.rationale: Janashakthi PLC is a diversified financial-services holding company with genuine operating franchises: Janashakthi Insurance PLC (77.58%, life insurance), Janashakthi Finance PLC (93.44%, NBFI/leasing) and First Capital Holdings PLC (76.57%, investment banking) -- both Life Insurance and NBFI segments were profitable this quarter even as the Group swung to a loss, evidencing underlying franchise value. A structural complexity limits assessment: the Life Insurance subsidiary is consolidated with a ~3-month reporting lag (31 March data used for a 30 June Group position) per its own differing fiscal year-end, and a December 2025 share subdivision was not retrospectively applied to the 2025 comparative EPS.

governance_risk.rationale: No circulars/disclosures feed exists to independently verify board or ownership changes. A mild disclosure-quality flag: the December 2025 2.84-for-1 share subdivision was not retrospectively applied to restate the Q1 FY2025/26 comparative EPS (still shown on the pre-subdivision base of 633,551,428 shares), materially distorting the reported YoY EPS comparison, though the underlying PAT figures are unaffected and clearly disclosed. The pending Continental Insurance Lanka acquisition (subject to IRCSL approval) is a material pending regulatory dependency.

key_reasons: The Rs.780.8mn Group net loss is a trading/markets story, not an insurance or lending problem: a Rs.2,229.3mn unfavourable FVTPL fair-value swing and a Rs.1,248.8mn Other Operating Income decline account for most of the deterioration, while Life Insurance and NBFI segments both remained profitable this quarter

P/B of ~1.66x (price Rs.11.00 vs parent-attributable NAV/share Rs.6.64) is a moderate multiple for a group with genuine insurance/NBFI/investment-banking franchises, though P/E is not meaningful this quarter given the net loss

A Rs.5.0bn IPO completed 29 April 2026 has funded a post-quarter Rs.5.2bn agreement to acquire Continental Insurance Lanka from Melstacorp PLC -- a material expansion of the insurance franchise, subject to IRCSL approval
watch_factors: Investment Banking segment (First Capital Holdings) posted the single largest current-quarter loss (Rs.689.3mn) on an Rs.87.95bn FVTPL portfolio -- earnings from this segment are inherently volatile and could swing positive or negative again next quarter
The Continental Insurance Lanka acquisition (Rs.5.2bn, 81% initial stake) is subject to IRCSL approval and integration risk -- a material unknown for the Group's insurance-segment trajectory

Reported EPS trend (Rs.2.38 to Rs.(0.30)) significantly overstates the economic decline due to a non-retrospectively-restated share subdivision and IPO dilution -- any future EPS-based screening of this stock needs to account for the distorted share-count base

horizon_notes.6m: Whether the Investment Banking segment's FVTPL losses reverse in Q2 FY2026/27, and early progress on IRCSL approval for the Continental Insurance Lanka acquisition, will be the key near-term signals.
horizon_notes.1y: A full year of segment performance (with Life Insurance and NBFI's underlying profitability as the base case) should clarify how much of this quarter's loss was genuinely one-off trading volatility.
horizon_notes.3y: Thesis depends on successful integration of Continental Insurance Lanka and whether the Investment Banking segment's earnings volatility can be managed without recurring large losses.
horizon_notes.5y: No macro/insurance-regulatory data source in this project to assess a multi-year Sri Lankan insurance/financial-services sector outlook for JXG's expanded franchise.

interim_updates.note_text: Janashakthi PLC (JXG) reported a Group net loss of Rs.780.77mn for Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026), against a Rs.2,180.61mn profit a year earlier, on Revenue of Rs.6,400.18mn (-11.6% YoY from Rs.7,239.29mn). JXG fully consolidates its subsidiaries at Group level -- Janashakthi Insurance PLC (77.58%, life insurance), Janashakthi Finance PLC (93.44%, NBFI/leasing) and First Capital Holdings PLC (76.57%, investment banking/primary dealer) -- so Group revenue is genuine trading income (premiums, interest, investment-banking activity), not an equity pickup; that equity-pickup dynamic instead dominates the separate COMPANY (standalone) result -- see below. The swing to a Group net loss was driven predominantly by two items: a Rs.2,229.33mn unfavourable swing in the Change in fair value of financial assets at FVTPL, from a Rs.1,256.46mn GAIN in Q1 FY2025/26 to a Rs.972.87mn LOSS in Q1 FY2026/27, on the Group's Rs.87,951.34mn FVTPL portfolio; and a Rs.1,248.75mn drop in Other Operating Income (Rs.114.36mn vs Rs.1,363.11mn, -91.6%) -- together roughly 74% of the Rs.4,707.85mn swing in Profit/(Loss) from operations (Rs.(1,248.68)mn vs Rs.3,459.18mn). Net insurance benefits, claims and life-fund movements also rose 25.0% YoY to Rs.2,506.41mn (2025: Rs.2,005.58mn), and Administrative & other operating expenses rose 9.3% to Rs.1,598.16mn (2025: Rs.1,462.36mn). By segment (Note 8, current quarter only, no 2025 comparator disclosed): Investment Banking (First Capital Holdings) was the single largest contributor to the loss, at Rs.(689.29)mn, followed by 'Other' at Rs.(366.50)mn, while Life Insurance (Rs.234.06mn) and NBFI (Rs.90.41mn) segments both remained profitable this quarter -- the loss is concentrated in the investment-banking/trading book, not the insurance or lending franchises. Partially offsetting the operating deterioration, Net finance income/(cost) swung favourably by Rs.713.35mn (to Rs.304.57mn net income from a Rs.408.78mn net expense) as Finance income surged to Rs.764.10mn (2025: Rs.12.04mn), and Income tax swung from a Rs.869.78mn expense to a Rs.163.34mn net credit/reversal, a Rs.1,033.13mn favourable swing. Basic EPS of Rs.(0.30) vs Rs.2.38 a year earlier looks dramatic but is NOT like-for-like: the Company raised Rs.5,000mn via an IPO of 500,000,000 new shares on 29 April 2026 (within this quarter), and separately effected a 2.84-for-1 share subdivision on 31 December 2025 whose effect was NOT retrospectively applied to restate the 2025 comparative EPS (which still uses the pre-subdivision base of 633,551,428 shares) -- so a material share of the apparent EPS decline is a share-count base effect, not economic profit decline; the PAT swing itself (-780.77mn vs +2,180.61mn) is the cleaner comparison. At the standalone COMPANY level, the result is dominated by the equity-accounted 'Share of profit/(loss) from equity accounted investee', which swung from a Rs.2,097.84mn GAIN to a Rs.241.51mn LOSS (a Rs.2,339.35mn swing) -- this single line explains essentially all of the Company's PBT swing (Rs.(617.09)mn vs Rs.1,509.68mn) and confirms JXG's standalone P&L is fundamentally an equity-pickup of its subsidiaries' results rather than trading revenue (Company Revenue was a nominal Rs.76.62mn this quarter). One further important structural caveat: per the filing's own footnote, Janashakthi Insurance PLC's 31 March 2026 financial information (not 30 June 2026) was used for Group consolidation because of its 31 December financial year-end -- i.e. the Life Insurance segment (39% of quarter Revenue) is consolidated with a roughly 3-month lag in every quarter, a structural feature of this filing rather than a one-off gap. Subsequent to quarter-end (13 August 2026), JXG signed a Share Purchase Agreement with Melstacorp PLC to acquire 100% of Continental Insurance Lanka Limited for LKR5.2bn (81% initial stake, then 9%/10% in years one/two), subject to IRCSL approval -- a material insurance-sector acquisition, plausibly funded in part by the April 2026 IPO proceeds.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: this is the first financial_statements entry for JXG, no prior quarter collected. Segment note (Note 8, page 10) discloses ONLY the current quarter (30.06.2026) with no 2025 comparator column, so no YoY segment-level revenue/profit comparison is possible from this filing -- current-quarter segment splits were cited in note_text/highlights as the best available specific attribution, but a true YoY segment waterfall is a genuine filing-level gap. current_assets/current_liabilities are not populated: the Statement of Financial Position does not present a current/ non-current subtotal split (standard for insurers/financial-services groups presenting assets/liabilities by order of liquidity), so these fields are structurally unavailable from this filing format, not omitted in error. Securities sold under repurchase agreements (Rs.52,768,305k, Group), Deposits from customers (Rs.17,771,774k, Group) and Debentures (Rs.7,316,156k, Group) are material disclosed funding lines specific to a financial-services group that are NOT folded into short_term_borrowings/long_term_borrowings (which map only to the face BS 'Interest bearing loans & borrowings' line, split via Note 7) to avoid mischaracterising distinct funding sources -- their magnitudes are cited in the GROUP row's notes field instead. eps_basic/eps_diluted YoY comparability is compromised by a 31 Dec 2025 share subdivision (2.84-for-1) that was NOT retrospectively applied to the 2025 comparative EPS, plus a mid-quarter (29 April 2026) IPO diluting the weighted-average share count -- both are quantified in the GROUP row's notes and flagged again here since they materially affect any EPS trend-reading. Janashakthi Insurance PLC (the largest segment) is consolidated with a structural ~3-month reporting lag (31 March 2026 data used for the 30 June 2026 Group position) -- disclosed by the filing itself, not resolved by this entry.
interim_updates.takeaway: JXG's swing to a Rs.780.77mn Group net loss is a markets/trading story, not an insurance or lending problem: a Rs.2,229.33mn unfavourable FVTPL fair-value swing plus a Rs.1,248.75mn drop in Other Operating Income together explain roughly three-quarters of the operating deterioration, and the current-quarter segment split shows the loss concentrated in the Investment Banking segment (Rs.689.29mn loss) while Life Insurance and NBFI both stayed profitable. The reported EPS collapse (Rs.2.38 to Rs.(0.30)) significantly overstates the economic decline because the 2025 comparator was not restated for the December 2025 share subdivision and the current quarter carries a diluted weighted-average share count from the April 2026 IPO -- the PAT swing is the more reliable read. Longer-term, the balance sheet shows a Company fundamentally built around its equity-accounted insurance/finance/investment-banking stakes (70.5% of standalone assets), now moving toward further insurance-sector expansion via the post-quarter Continental Insurance Lanka acquisition agreement, partly funded by the Rs.5,000mn IPO raised this quarter.

Investment Banking segment (First Capital Holdings) posted the largest current-quarter segment loss, Rs.689.29mn, while Life Insurance (+Rs.234.06mn) and NBFI (+Rs.90.41mn) segments stayed profitable -- loss is concentrated in the trading/investment-banking book.
Partially offsetting: Finance income +Rs.752.06mn YoY to Rs.764.10mn, and a Rs.1,033.13mn favourable tax swing (Rs.869.78mn expense to Rs.163.34mn credit).

thesis.thesis_text: Janashakthi PLC is a financial-services holding company that fully consolidates Janashakthi Insurance PLC (77.58%, life insurance), Janashakthi Finance PLC (93.44%, NBFI/leasing) and First Capital Holdings PLC (76.57%, investment banking/primary dealer). Group swung to a Rs.780.8mn net loss in Q1 FY2026/27 (from a Rs.2,180.6mn profit a year earlier), driven by a Rs.2,229.3mn unfavourable swing in FVTPL fair-value gains and a Rs.1,248.8mn drop in Other Operating Income -- concentrated in the Investment Banking segment (Rs.689.3mn loss), while Life Insurance (+Rs.234.1mn) and NBFI (+Rs.90.4mn) stayed profitable. The reported EPS collapse (Rs.2.38 to Rs.(0.30)) is not like-for-like given an unrestated December 2025 share subdivision and a mid-quarter IPO, so the underlying PAT swing is the cleaner read. At Rs.11.00, P/B (on parent-attributable equity, Rs.6.64/share NAV) is a moderate 1.66x; the Group is now pursuing a material post-quarter acquisition of Continental Insurance Lanka for Rs.5.2bn, subject to regulatory approval (Q1 FY2026/27 filing, source_doc_id 52751).
